slides.texte_overlay:
7 Social Hacks That Feel
Like Cheating
When you walk into a party where you know nobody, offer to help the host. Carrying drinks or handing out plates gives you a reason to talk to everyone.
When someone gives you a compliment, don't deflect it. Just smile and say "Thank you, that's kind." Accepting it gracefully makes you look confident.
When a group chat goes quiet after you suggest a plan, pick a date yourself. "Saturday at 7, I'll book." Clear decisions get people to show up.
When you meet someone's partner for the first time, ask how they met. Couples love telling that story, and it instantly makes you feel like an old friend.
When the conversation stalls, share a surprising fact. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, so I always have something that gets people talking.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I always have a surprising fact that gets people talking.

slides.texte_overlay: When you need a favour from a busy person, make it tiny and specific. "Could you look at one slide for two minutes?" Small asks get fast yeses.
When you're late, don't over-explain. "Sorry I'm late, thanks for waiting." A short, sincere apology is better than five minutes of excuses.
